preamble: Click insertion in an inherited Nguni word. Wiktionary derives Zulu and Xhosa -cambalala 'lie down, recline, lie on the stomach' (c = dental click [ǀ]) from Proto-Bantu *-dàmbadada, a double extensive of *-dàmba 'sprawl'. The source just calls the word inherited and does not say whether hlonipha avoidance or another mechanism was involved. This is a sporadic, lexically specific replacement within the wider adoption of Khoisan clicks into Nguni (Pakendorf et al. 2017, cited in Sands & Gunnink 2019), not a regular sound change. The etymology rests on the Wiktionary cambalala entry alone: Wiktionary's own *-dàmba page glosses that root as 'be starved' and lists only a Sotho reflex. Only one etymon is attested (Zulu and Xhosa share it), so certainty is 2.

examples.to: Zulu -cambalala 'lie down, recline'; Xhosa -cambalala 'lie on the stomach'
examples.note: Wiktionary, citing the Zulu–English Dictionary. One etymon in two closely related languages.

sources: Herbert, R. K. (1990). Hlonipha and the ambiguous woman. Anthropos 85, 455–473 (cited in Wikipedia: Avoidance speech).
